punchline: In Harari's account, happiness depends less on what you have than on what you expected: wanting a Ferrari and getting a Fiat feels like loss.
thirty_sec: Harari asks whether we are happier than people before us. Researchers measure it with questionnaires scored from 0 to 10, and what shows up is that expectations count more than conditions. Someone who wanted a Ferrari and got a used Fiat feels deprived. In a study by Kahneman, parents found raising children full of unpleasant moments yet called them their main source of happiness. Harari says happiness comes from seeing your life as meaningful.
